name: E. coli bacterium
headline: length
description: Escherichia coli is a rod-shaped bacterium that lives in the gut and is one of the most studied organisms in biology. Its shape is close to a cylinder with rounded ends. A widely used rule of thumb puts a cell at about 2 µm long and 1 µm wide, with a volume near 1 cubic micrometre and a mass of about a picogram, though cell size changes with growth conditions.

measures.label: Length
measures.note: Rule-of-thumb cell length based on light and electron microscopy

measures.label: Volume
measures.note: Stated as about 1 µm³ (1 fL); 1 µm³ = 1e-12 cm³. Volumes range from about 0.4 to 2.5 µm³ depending on growth rate

measures.label: Mass
measures.note: Stated as about 1 pg (1e-12 g), estimated from the 1 µm³ volume at the density of water

facts.text: Faster-growing cells are larger: E. coli dry mass differs about five-fold between slow- and fast-growing cultures.
Treating the cell as a cylinder with hemispherical caps, 1 µm wide and 2 µm long, gives a volume of about 1.3 µm³.

sources.publisher: Cell Biology by the Numbers (Milo and Phillips)
sources.title: How big is an E. coli cell and what is its mass?

caveats: The source presents these as rules of thumb and notes that laboratories do not always agree; size varies with strain and growth rate.
Volume and mass are converted exactly from the source's µm³ and pg because those units are not in the site's unit list.
